newsitem.title: USA: Most U.S. stock index futures end lower on bonds.
newsitem.headline: Most U.S. stock index futures end lower on bonds.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures ended mostly lower in sympathy with the sell-off in the U.S. bond market, traders said.

June Standard & Poor's 500 futures fell to a session low of 832.20 in the afternoon soon after U.S. bond futures dipped on a Reuters story quoting sources close to the Federal Reserve as saying the Fed was likely to raise the federal funds rate by 25 basis points on Tuesday, May 20.
Comments by Richmond Federal Reserve president Alfred Broaddus that the U.S. economy was expanding rapidly and labor markets will remain tight were also considered bearish.
Despite the selloff in U.S. bonds and stocks, most S&P futures traders said this week's price action points to further all-time record highs for June S&Ps.
"This trend is obviously up," Kevin O'Brien, a short-term technical analyst for Prudential Securities, said.
"It's proven itself with these run-ups, but the thing that concerns me is the light volume and open interest, which is not expanding on the highs," he said.
O'Brien also expressed some concern about the U.S. bond futures market.
He said a rise to 111-00 in June T-bonds might improve the trend.
June S&Ps closed above fair value, which is currently at 2.75 points.

At the end of pit trade, June S&Ps were off 3.50 at 837.85, KCBT Value Lines were off 1.75 at 733.30, NYSE Composites were down 1.75 at 435.85, Nikkeis were off 65 at 20,215, Midcap 400s were 1.35 lower at 269.70, Russell 2000s were up 0.50 at 366.25 and Nasdaq 100s were down 11.50 at 918.75.
